meta.description: Daily tracking state for F-1/SEVP/DS-2019 policy monitoring, focused on relevance to a Virginia Tech student who may need an extra semester to finish their degree.

items.title: DHS Final Rule: Fixed Time Period of Admission & Extension of Stay (ends Duration of Status) for F, J, I nonimmigrants
items.summary: DHS published a final rule (doc. 2026-14439) on Jul 17, 2026, ending open-ended Duration of Status for F-1 students, effective Sep 15, 2026. Students get a fixed 'Admit Until Date' capped at 4 years (24 months for language programs); anyone needing more time must file Form I-539 (Extension of Stay) with USCIS in addition to the existing DSO SEVIS extension. A timely-filed EOS gives up to 240 days of authorized stay while pending. The rule also shortens the F-1 post-completion grace period from 60 to 30 days for anyone who travels/re-enters or gets an EOS approval after the effective date.
items.notes: No lawsuit had been filed and no Congressional Review Act disapproval resolution had passed as of this run (checked 2026-08-11); coverage still describes litigation/CRA action as 'possible' or 'expected,' not filed. NAFSA remains publicly opposed. SEVP has a stakeholder webinar scheduled Mon, Aug 31, 2026, 2-3pm ET to walk through the rule (per secondary reporting; studyinthestates.dhs.gov and ice.gov could not be fetched directly again this run).

items.title: USCIS Policy Alert PA-2026-05: officers may deny incomplete filings without issuing an RFE/NOID first
items.summary: Effective Aug 5, 2026, USCIS updated Policy Manual guidance so adjudicators may, at their discretion, deny a benefit request lacking required initial evidence or failing to establish eligibility without first issuing an RFE or NOID, and may set RFE response deadlines shorter than the prior 12-week norm (the 14-day international-mail grace period was also eliminated). Directly relevant to F-1 students filing Form I-539 (Extension of Stay) or I-765 under the new fixed-admission-period regime: an incomplete EOS package can now be denied outright with no chance to cure.
items.notes: Could not reach uscis.gov/policy-manual directly again this run (network egress to uscis.gov is blocked in this environment) to pull the actual Policy Alert PA-2026-05 text/citation. Multiple additional law-firm sources now corroborate the Aug 5, 2026 effective date and substance, but none is an official .gov citation. Will keep retrying uscis.gov each run to move this to Confirmed.

items.title: DHS regulatory review of OPT / STEM OPT (RIN 1653-AA97) — no NPRM published yet
items.summary: DHS confirmed in a Jan 9, 2026 letter it is re-evaluating the scope and duration of OPT and STEM OPT, with a rulemaking entry (RIN 1653-AA97) in the Spring 2026 Unified Regulatory Agenda covering worker protection, fraud prevention, national security, and SEVP oversight goals. As of this run, no Notice of Proposed Rulemaking has been published in the Federal Register; secondary reporting still describes the rule as pre-proposal, with a full rulemaking process typically taking 12-24+ months. OPT and STEM OPT remain fully operational and unchanged today. Relevant because many students planning an extra semester are also relying on post-completion OPT/STEM OPT timing.
items.notes: Could not reach reginfo.gov or federalregister.gov directly this run to confirm the RIN 1653-AA97 unified-agenda entry text (both blocked). No OPT/STEM OPT NPRM exists yet to cite as of 2026-08-11. Will keep watching for actual NPRM publication.
